The Receptionist
Role Profile — Responsibilities, Front Desk & Hygiene
The first impression, the last impression, and every moment between.
Reports to: Front Desk Manager   ·   Coordinates with: Counsellor · Doctor · Housekeeping
Version 1.0

blocks.title: Slide 2
blocks.text:
01 · ROLE PURPOSE
The face of the branch — held at both ends of the day
The Receptionist is the first and the last impression of the clinic.
Every client is greeted, booked, attended and billed through the front desk — and the warmth, accuracy and discipline of that desk shape how the whole visit feels. The receptionist owns the front desk: greeting, appointments, calls, hospitality coordination, billing and records — to the standard the brand expects.
Reception is not a back-office function. A client decides how they feel about the clinic in the first ten seconds at the desk, and in the last ten seconds at billing. Hold both with the same care.
IN ONE SENTENCE
“Greet every client warmly, never lose an enquiry, keep the desk and the data clean, and make every payment transparent.”
The doctor is the reason she came.
You are the reason she stayed.

PART TWO
Front Desk Responsibilities
Every working day follows one rhythm — the discipline is what makes the desk run.

blocks.title: Slide 9
blocks.text:
04 · STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE
The daily rhythm — morning, through the day, evening
Morning
BEFORE CLIENTS ARRIVE
Review the full day's schedule; keep the booking dashboard open
Ready the desk — forms, cards, stationery; check CRM, billing, phone, AC, lighting, music
Confirm with housekeeping: reception, washrooms & water station ready
Join the reception huddle with the FDM
Through the Day
GREET · ATTEND · BILL
Greet within 10s by name; locate by name and check in
Offer water / tea / coffee; communicate any wait proactively
Answer every call; keep the callback log; send WhatsApp confirmations
Bill transparently — state amount & purpose, send receipt, record accurately
Evening
AFTER CLIENTS LEAVE
Confirm tomorrow's appointments and send confirmations
Complete all callbacks in the log
Reconcile & close billing with the FDM; hand over cash securely
Update the CRM; tidy and lock the desk

blocks.title: Slide 10
blocks.text:
05 · SIGNATURE STANDARDS
The habits that make GLEUHR feel different
The 10-second rule
A client is greeted, by name, within ten seconds of walking in — warmth before paperwork.
Find by name — never “your number”
Appointments are located by the client's name — asking for a phone number first makes a client feel like a record, not a guest.
THE THREE AFFIRMATIONS
1
WELCOME
“Welcome to GLEUHR. Please come in.”
2
THE WAIT
“Thank you for your patience. She'll be with you in just a few minutes.”
3
THE GOODBYE
“Call us anytime, for anything. That's what we're here for.”

blocks.title: Slide 11
blocks.text:
06 · THE PATIENT JOURNEY
Reading the moment — and holding it well
Phone enquiry
Pick up by the third ring. Offer to hold a slot, not chase a booking. Give your name — turn an enquiry into a small relationship.
The walk-in welcome
Be on her side of the desk, in her eye-line, glad to see her. The first eight seconds set how everything later lands.
The wait
The most fragile time. Acknowledge it — “thank you for your patience.” Being seen resets the whole mood, even if the wait doesn't shorten.
The nervous / new patient
Orient her calmly — this is normal. 45 seconds of reassurance saves the doctor five minutes inside.
The complaint
Hear · believe · help — in that order. Listen first 60 seconds. Never argue; move it private; escalate to FDM/BM when needed.
The goodbye
Walk her out, use her name, open the door. The 30 seconds at the door buys the next referral.

blocks.title: Slide 12
blocks.text:
07 · BILLING, RECORDS & CRM
Where trust and accuracy meet
Every payment, transparent
State the amount and purpose before you collect. Generate the bill and send the receipt to the client's WhatsApp. Record it accurately, every time.
Records clean, forms complete
Keep contact and WhatsApp details accurate. Complete the registration form for every client. Tag every lead and log every enquiry — CRM accuracy at 100%.
ABSOLUTE RED LINES
Zero off-system or cash-in-hand payments
Billing accuracy at 100% — no errors, no disputes
A WhatsApp receipt for every single payment
Client data never shared improperly

blocks.title: Slide 13

PART THREE
Clinic Cleaning & Hygiene Responsibility
The desk owns the first thing a client sees — a clean, calm, welcoming front of house.

blocks.title: Slide 14
blocks.text:
08 · FRONT-OF-HOUSE HYGIENE
Reception's cleaning & hygiene duties, through the day
Opening
BEFORE CLIENTS ARRIVE
Confirm with housekeeping: reception, washrooms & water station clean and ready
Desk wiped and tidy; card machine, phone & pens sanitized
Waiting area arranged; seating clean; brochures neat
Entrance hand-sanitizer filled; floor clean; bins lined
Through the Day
KEEP IT GUEST-READY
Wipe the counter & card machine between clients
2-hourly washroom & water-station check with housekeeping
Clear cups/clutter from waiting area promptly; flag any spill
Keep sanitizer, tissues & water stocked at the front
Closing
SET UP TOMORROW
Clear and wipe the desk & billing/cash area
Ensure waiting area reset and bins emptied with housekeeping
Confirm washrooms cleaned & restocked for next day
Final walkthrough — front of house clean, calm, locked

blocks.title: Slide 15
blocks.text:
08 · HYGIENE — OWNERSHIP
What Reception owns, and what it coordinates
RECEPTION OWNS DIRECTLY
The reception desk — tidy, wiped, uncluttered
Billing / card / cash area cleanliness
Front-desk high-touch points sanitized
Water station stocked & presentable
Personal grooming & uniform to standard
COORDINATES WITH HOUSEKEEPING
Waiting-area comfort & cleanliness
Washroom readiness & 2-hourly checks
Floors, glass doors & general cleaning
Air quality, freshener & ambience
Reporting any lapse before clients notice
Hygiene is a shared standard: Reception is the eyes of the front of house and raises anything that isn't guest-ready — it does not wait to be told.

11 · THE NEVER LIST
Standards that hold — however busy the desk
✕
Never take an off-system or cash-in-hand payment
✕
Never lose, ignore or fail to log an enquiry
✕
Never share client data improperly
✕
Never argue with a client — acknowledge and escalate
✕
Never leave the desk unattended without cover
✕
Never use a personal phone at the desk in front of clients
✕
Never advise a client on a clinical matter
✕

✕

✕

blocks.title: Slide 19
blocks.text:
12 · CONSEQUENCES FRAMEWORK
Fair, documented, and proportionate
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with the FDM; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months, same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR + FDM
Lost / unlogged enquiries, repeatedly
Written warning
Billing error or dispute, repeatedly
Written warning; billing re-training
Single off-system payment / data mishandling
Same-day review; termination consideration
Serious dishonesty with the FDM
Single-incident termination consideration
